There is no reported brake-fluid flush in 10 years and two multi-year gaps with no reported entries. Absence is not proof the work was skipped, but nothing time-based is shown.

CARFAX gives the build as 06/27/2016, inside the higher-risk early-ND1 6MT window. There is no reported transmission repair or warranty entry and no door-jamb build-date photo. Gearbox health is unproven.
This is a soft-top car kept 10 years in Illinois. No photos of lifted footwell carpet, the drain area behind the seats or the seat-rail bolts are among those examined here.

CARFAX says 'No open recalls reported to CARFAX', which is not a dealer printout or NHTSA VIN lookup. Two recalls apply: 19V496 (2016 skid plate and bracket) and 24V695 (airbag control module software). 19V072 applies to automatics only and is not relevant. No Mazda-dealer visit is reported in the history, so completion is not shown.

CARFAX shows 'Battery replaced' at the selling dealer on 10/16/2026 and 'Tire(s) replaced' at Car-X on 04/11/2022. These are dated report entries. Tire DOT codes were not examined here and should still be confirmed.

documentation.rationale: The identity half is strong: published VIN, clean decode, CARFAX with guaranteed clean title, one owner and consistent mileage. The maintenance half is thin. There are four undetailed service entries, two multi-year gaps, no brake-fluid or coolant record, no transmission history and no owner receipts.

condition.rationale: Photos show straight, clean-looking paint and a tidy tan interior with light driver-bolster creasing. The dealer PDI replaced the battery, air filter and oil and 'serviced' the brakes. The underside of a 10-year Illinois car, the gearbox of a mid-2016 build, top drains and fabric, and warning lights with the engine running are all unexamined.

price_value.rationale: At $20,819 the asking price is roughly 15% above the mileage-adjusted fair value of $17,589 to $18,271 for 2016-2018 soft-top ND1s. Active peers include a 2017 RF Grand Touring with 13k miles asking $21,450. The recent $1,000 cut narrows but does not close the gap.

mission_fit.rationale: It is a manual, reliable, inexpensive-to-run roadster well inside the budget band, so it plausibly solves the bridge. Two points hold it back: it is a soft top rather than the preferred RF for year-round rain use, and it is an early-build ND1 with unproven gearbox history.

logistics.rationale: Champaign, IL is about 2,100 miles away. A franchise dealer should accommodate a mobile PPI, but access is not stated. A fly-and-drive home is feasible, and CA smog and registration for a 2016 gasoline car with over 7,500 miles should be routine.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Machine Gray-looking paint (his top colour) with tan leather in a stock Grand Touring manual is a desirable combination. Against that, it is a soft top rather than RF, the 155 hp ND1 rather than the 181 hp ND2, there is no evidence of the LSD or Bilstein package, and the interior is tan rather than Auburn.

ppi_focus: Gearbox: cold and fully warm shifts through every gear, with special attention to 2nd/3rd grinding and pop-outs under load and overrun on this mid-2016 build. Also check fluid condition.
Clutch: slip test in 4th-6th under load, engagement height, and hydraulic or pedal noises.
Underside corrosion from 10 Illinois winters: subframes, brake and fuel lines, exhaust hangers, rocker seams, suspension fasteners.
Water ingress: soft-top drains flowed, carpet underlay dry, no musty smell, no seat-rail bolt corrosion, floor connectors clean.
Soft-top fabric at the rear-corner fold points and header seal, plus a water test if possible.
Brake-fluid moisture test, and verification of whatever brake work the PDI actually did.
Water pump weep hole, and coolant level and condition (no record of a change in 10 years).
Oil seepage at the valve cover, timing cover and front crank seal, and the rear diff pinion and output seals.
Full OBD and airbag scan with engine running; confirm the skid plate and bracket are secure (recall 19V496).
Tire DOT codes, even wear (alignment), aluminum hood and fender dents, nose chips or respray, and Mazda Connect screen ghost-touch.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: a clean PPI with a dry, solid underside, a gearbox smooth through 2nd/3rd when warm, and no water history.
Up: dealer price movement toward the $17.6k-$18.3k fair-value band, or a PPI-funded catch-up of fluids.
Up: owner receipts or a recall printout showing brake fluid and coolant service and recall completion.
Down: any grinding or popping out of gear, clutch slip, significant underbody corrosion, damp carpet or a worn-through top.
Down: dealer refusal of a mobile PPI before deposit.
evidence.mission_note: A stock, one-owner Grand Touring manual in his preferred gray is a plausible low-cost enthusiast bridge within budget. It is the less-preferred soft-top ND1, with an early-build gearbox to verify, rather than the RF or ND2 he is targeting.
evidence.rationale: The CARFAX establishes a clean, guaranteed title, one personal Illinois owner for 10 years, no reported accidents, and mileage that matches the cluster photo at 34,462. The service record is thin: four undetailed entries with gaps of about four and three years. There is no reported brake-fluid, coolant or gearbox-fluid service, and the only explicit oil change is the selling dealer's 10/16/2026 PDI, which also replaced the battery. The car was built 06/27/2016, inside the early ND1 6MT risk window, and no transmission history or door-jamb photo is provided. Photos show a straight, apparently stock gray car with tan leather and only light driver-bolster creasing. The underside after 10 Illinois winters, cabin water history and soft-top fabric remain unexamined. At $20,819 the asking price sits above the mileage-adjusted fair value of $17,589 to $18,271 for soft-top ND1s, and a 2017 RF Grand Touring peer is asking $21,450. Recall closure for 19V496 and 24V695 rests only on CARFAX's 'no open recalls reported'.
evidence.next_action: Email the dealer for four things before arranging anything else: an out-the-door price, the itemized 10/16/2026 PDI repair order, a Mazda/NHTSA recall printout, and written permission for a mobile PPI in Champaign.
